messages:
alex kim: Hi! New hire here, trying to get local services running. On an M1 Mac with Docker Desktop. postgres container keeps crashing during init with permission denied on the mounted volume. 😕

alex kim: docker-compose up stops with this: 
```
postgres_1  | initdb: could not create directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata": Permission denied
postgres_1  |   (Detail: failed to create directory)
postgres_1  | The files belonging to this database system will be owned by user "postgres".
```

alex kim: I tried chmod/chown on the host folder but it's a mac volume mount so it doesn't stick. Anyone hit this? Who should I ping?

maria (eng): hey alex, welcome! :wave: This is pretty common on macOS with bind mounts + postgres because the container user expects certain ownership. Two quick options: use a named docker volume instead of bind-mounting a host dir, or initialize the data dir from the container as root once and chown.

maria (eng): Example: 
```bash
# create a named volume and use that in compose
docker volume create redwood_dev_pgdata
# then in compose replace ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data with redwood_dev_pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
```

sam s: +1 to named volume. Our repo has a helper: `scripts/setup-local-db.sh` that will create the volume and run migrations. Try `./scripts/setup-local-db.sh --force`

alex kim: thanks — tried named volume, postgres starts but my app can't connect: connection refused. Logs show postgres listening on unix socket only?

ben (infra): on M1 you might be hitting the linux/arm vs amd64 image mismatch. Are you using the official postgres image or a pinned sha? `docker inspect <container>` and check the architecture.

alex kim: how do I force arm image if docker pulled amd64?

maria (eng): you can add `platform: linux/arm64` to the service in docker-compose.override.yml to force the arm build. But prefer using images that support multi-arch. Also check `postgres` env var `PGDATA` — we mount to `/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata` in our compose, make sure app uses same path/credentials from .env.example.

ops-bot: Helpful docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/dev-setup#postgres-local (internal link) :link:

sam s: also if you see socket-only listen, check `postgres` env `listen_addresses='*'` in the compose envs and map the port `5432:5432`. Example snippet from our repo: 
```yaml
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:15
    platform: linux/arm64
    volumes:
      - redwood_dev_pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: redwood
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: localpass
      POSTGRES_DB: redwood_dev
      PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
    ports:
      - 5432:5432
volumes:
  redwood_dev_pgdata:
    driver: local
```

alex kim: okay that helped — after switching to named volume + platform: linux/arm64 postgres started and app connects. One remaining weirdness: `psql` as host user can't access files inside volume, so `./scripts/db-reset` fails. Any best practice?

maria (eng): for CLI db ops we wrap commands inside the container. e.g. `docker compose exec postgres psql -U redwood -d redwood_dev -c "SELECT 1;"` or run a temporary helper container mounting the same volume. We avoid relying on host fs perms for DB files.

alex kim: perfect — thanks everyone! Tagging this as resolved for my setup. Appreciate the quick help :tada:

ben (infra): pro tip: if you prefer host-based DB for speed, use Postgres installed via Homebrew and set app DATABASE_URL to `postgres://...` in .env.local, but team standard is containerized so we can reproduce CI.

maria (eng): adding to onboarding checklist: note about M1 and `platform` flag + prefer named volumes. I'll open a tiny PR to docs.

alex kim: awesome, thanks again :heart:
